researcher_notes:
COMPANY CONFIRMED REAL. Seegrid Corporation, 216 RIDC Park West Drive, Pittsburgh, PA 15275, USA (address verified verbatim on the back cover of the archived Seegrid Palion Tow Tractor brochure PDF). Country: USA. Founded 2003 by roboticist Hans Moravec and Scott Friedman. Long-established vision-guided AGV/AMR OEM (>20 M autonomous miles, >200 customer sites per seegrid.com/safety). Sales model: direct (Seegrid ended its Raymond distribution partnership).

CURRENT CATALOGUE: exactly 4 vehicle products, verified against the full page sitemap (https://seegrid.com/page-sitemap.xml, retrieved 2026-08-01): Lift EL1, Lift RS1, Lift CR1, Tow Tractor S7. All 4 are in scope (pallet / cart transport vehicles). No rack-integrated or software-only products were counted; Fleet Central / Supervisor / Fleet Geek are fleet software and Autonomous Buffer Management (ABM) is a workflow product - all correctly excluded.

DISCONTINUED / RENAMED: the former 'Palion' brand prefix (Palion Lift, Palion Pallet Truck Series 8, Palion Tow Tractor Series 8) has been retired from seegrid.com. The standalone Palion Pallet Truck (end-rider low-lift pallet truck) no longer has a product page and appears to have been superseded by the Lift EL1 - it is NOT included here because it cannot be confirmed as currently sold.

DATA AVAILABILITY: Seegrid publishes only a short 'Key Specifications' block per product page; full spec sheets are behind a HubSpot lead-capture form ('Download X Specs' / 'See All Product Specs' are lightbox forms, no public PDF). The current 'Complete Fleet Brochure.pdf' on hub.seegrid.com now returns HTTP 404. The ONLY full public spec table found is the archived Palion Tow Tractor brochure (Wayback Machine) - used for the S7 with an explicit staleness flag (see that product's notes).

UNIT CONVENTION: Seegrid publishes exclusively in US customary units (lbs, feet/inches, mph, degF). All values below converted to project canonical units (kg, mm, m/s, degC); each conversion is shown in the product notes.

ALLOWED-VALUE NOTE: values below use the ACTUAL AP0 allowed_values from config/fields.json, which differ slightly from the vocabulary in the research brief - AP0 has separate 'Pallet EUR' and 'Pallet ISO' (not a combined 'Pallet EUR/ISO'), and 'Limited 3D (e.g. waterfall)'. AP0 industries_served has no 'Warehousing'/'Logistics' options, so Seegrid's stated industries were mapped to the nearest allowed values.

FLAGS / CONCERNS:
1. Seegrid's own RS1 page has a UNIT TYPO: the 'Key Specifications' block prints 'Max Lift Height: 6"' (inches). Everything else on Seegrid's own site says 6 FEET (hero banner, body copy, FAQ, /forkables/ page, /safety/ page). 6 ft is correct; 6 in would be implausible for a truck with a mast and ITA forks.
2. VDA 5050: only the Lift EL1 is stated as 'fully VDA 5050 2.1 compliant'. The company press release (July 2025) says foundational capabilities rolled out in 2025 with FULL compliance targeted for 2026 - i.e. it is a roadmap, not a per-model confirmation. vda5050_compatible therefore left NULL on RS1/CR1/S7 rather than assumed.
3. No public data at all for: aisle width (any model), stop/drop/pick accuracy, IP rating, cleanroom class, floor flatness class, fleet size limits, battery runtime, charge time, and all environmental specs for the three Lift models. All left NULL.
4. drive_type left NULL for all three Lift models. The AMR index page meta-describes the RS1 as an 'Autonomous Reach Truck', but the spec value 'Reach: 72"' equals exactly 6 ft = the stated lift height, so 'reach' there denotes VERTICAL reach, not a reach-truck mast stroke. Chassis class cannot be determined without contradiction - deliberately left NULL.

products.notes:
Hero: "5' 2\" LIFT HEIGHT | 2,500 LB LOAD CAPACITY"; Key Specifications block: Max Lift Height 5'2", Payload Capacity 2,500 lbs, Maximum Automatic Speed 3.4 mph, Safety 'Layered 2D & 3D LiDAR sensors', Forks 'ITA Rated; 42\" Standard, 36\"-48\" Optional'.
CONVERSIONS: 2500 lb x 0.45359237 = 1133.98 -> 1134 kg. 5'2" = 62 in x 25.4 = 1574.8 -> 1575 mm. 3.4 mph x 0.44704 = 1.5199 -> 1.52 m/s.
navigation_type: page states 'proprietary 3D computer vision, LiDAR/SLAM and payload detection technology'; FAQ 'navigates using infrastructure-free 3D LiDAR SLAM technology. It maps your facility digitally'. Both Vision and SLAM explicitly named -> both set.
infrastructure_free: FAQ 'Does the Lift EL1 require floor tape or magnets to navigate? No.' - explicit, HIGH.
vda5050_compatible / fleet_management_system: page states 'fully VDA 5050 2.1 compliant' three separate times incl. a dedicated FAQ. This is the ONLY Seegrid model with an explicit per-model VDA 5050 claim - HIGH.
safety_standard + safety_coverage: 'engineered to strictly adhere to ANSI B56.5 and ISO/IEC industrial autonomous vehicle safety standards, utilizing overlapping 3D sensor fields'. Note UL 583 (cited elsewhere by Seegrid for the tow tractor) is an electrical standard for battery-powered industrial trucks and was deliberately NOT mapped to AP0's 'UL 3100' (the AGV/AMR safety standard) - they are different standards.
manual_usage: CR1 FAQ states 'all of our AMRs are hybrid, meaning they use off-the-shelf chassis with custom-built Seegrid technology to allow for manual or autonomous operations' - line-wide statement, HIGH.
stacking_capability: MEDIUM. Not stated as a word, but derived: real mast lift of 1575 mm plus stated workflows 'Inbound to Putaway - transport payloads from inbound staging to bulk storage'. A 1.5 m mast places a second pallet level.
load_type: MEDIUM. /forkables/ page shows Seegrid Lift AMRs handling 48x40 (US GMA pallet, = ISO 6780 1219x1016 -> 'Pallet ISO'), plus 30x30, 96\"x78\" and 62\"x96\" non-pallet payloads -> 'Custom Carrier'. 'Pallet EUR' deliberately NOT set: 800x1200 mm Euro pallets are not evidenced for this US-market product and the 42\" standard fork would overhang the 800 mm face.
load_detection: /safety/ page 'It uses its vision system to identify and precisely locate the forkable pockets of the payload' + layered 2D/3D LiDAR -> Camera/Vision + Laser/LiDAR profiling. HIGH-MED.
integration_capability: MEDIUM. VDA5050 press coverage (July 2025) states 'Seegrid released a robust MQTT API that enables its AMRs to connect with today's industrial automation and orchestration systems'. Company-wide statement, not EL1-specific.
station_applications: MEDIUM, from the page's own workflow list: 'Pick + Drop from/to Wrappers, Conveyors, etc.' -> Conveyor; inbound/outbound staging on floor -> Floor; cross-docking -> Dock. 'Standard rack' NOT set (bulk/floor storage stated, racking not).
industries_served: page says 'space-constrained warehousing, 3PL facilities, and large retail fulfillment centers'. AP0 has no 'Warehousing' option -> mapped to 3PL + Retail only.
NOT FOUND (left NULL): vehicle dimensions, weight, battery type/runtime/charge time, autonomous_charging (Auto-Charge is documented for RS1/CR1/S7 but NOT mentioned on the EL1 page - deliberately not carried over), min_aisle_width, drive_type, mast_type, stop/drop/pick accuracy, all environmental specs, max_fleet_size.

Hero: "6' LIFT HEIGHT | 3,500 LB LOAD CAPACITY | 5 MPH". Forks: 'ITA Rated; 42\" Standard, 36\"-72\" Optional'.
CONVERSIONS: 3500 lb = 1587.57 -> 1588 kg. 6 ft = 1828.8 -> 1829 mm. 5 mph = 2.2352 -> 2.24 m/s.
LIFT HEIGHT DISCREPANCY RESOLVED: the page's Key Specifications block prints 'Max Lift Height: 6\"' (inches). This is a site typo. Four independent Seegrid statements say 6 FEET: hero banner "6' LIFT HEIGHT"; body 'automates vertical transport up to 6 feet'; FAQ 'featuring a 6-foot maximum lift height'; /forkables/ page "6' Lift Height"; /safety/ page 'low-lift workflow automation up to 6 feet'. Additionally the indexed spec line 'Reach: 72\"' = exactly 6 ft, independently confirming the vertical figure. Recorded as 1829 mm, HIGH confidence.
vehicle_width / vehicle_length: LOW CONFIDENCE. Values (Width 50\", Length 92\" forks retracted -> 1270 mm / 2336.8 -> 2337 mm) come from a Seegrid spec table that is indexed by search engines but whose source PDF (hub.seegrid.com/hubfs/Complete Fleet Brochure.pdf) now returns HTTP 404 and is not in the Wayback Machine, so it could not be re-verified first-hand. A second retrieval of the same source returned 'Reach: 6', Max Capacity: 4,000 lbs' for the RS1 - 4,000 lbs is the CR1 figure, proving the brochure is a MULTI-COLUMN table prone to column bleed in snippet extraction. Width/length were stable across both retrievals and are therefore retained, but flagged. RECOMMEND VERIFYING before use, or dropping to NULL if the DB operator prefers.
autonomous_obstacle_bypass: MEDIUM. FAQ: 'If a person steps into its path, the vehicle immediately stops OR dynamically adjusts its route.' Route adjustment is explicitly claimed, so set true - but note the archived Palion Tow Tractor brochure documents Seegrid's older standard safety behaviour as pure stop-and-resume, so this is a newer-generation ('Dynamic Path Planning') capability and the wording is not unambiguous.
safety_coverage: FAQ '360-degree safety coverage using overlapping 3D safety fields'; /safety/ page 'Lift RS1 provides 360-degree safety coverage'. HIGH.
autonomous_charging: page section 'Synchronized Self-Charging - Auto-Charge automates scheduling, dispatch, and charging'. HIGH.
navigation_type: 'proprietary computer-vision technology'; CR1 FAQ confirms RS1 and CR1 use the 'same core LiDAR/SLAM and 3D computer vision sensor suites'. /technology/ page: '2D and 3D LiDAR sensors, stereo cameras, and a proprietary computer vision system', 'proprietary Grid Engine ... 3D occupancy grid mapping'. HIGH.
infrastructure_free: dedicated page section 'Infrastructure-Free - deploy without changes to your facility'. HIGH.
stacking_capability / load_type / load_detection / station_applications / integration_capability: same derivations as the Lift EL1 entry - see there.
industries_served: page workflow tabs are 'Manufacturing' and 'Logistics'; body 'heavy manufacturing', 'high-throughput warehouse logistics' -> General Manufacturing + 3PL.
fleet_management_system: 'Proprietary' (Fleet Central). NOT set to 'VDA 5050 compatible' because no per-model VDA5050 claim exists for the RS1 - see researcher_notes flag 2.
OTHER PUBLISHED FACTS not mappable to AP0 fields: 5 safety-rated 2D/3D LiDAR sensors, 3 emergency stop buttons, LED lightbar, acoustic warning system, safety-rated personnel detection system, polyurethane wheels, lead time 26 weeks, Material Handling 2025 Products of the Year Readers' Choice Award.

Hero: "15' LIFT HEIGHT | 4,000 LB LOAD CAPACITY | 5.0 MPH"; Key Specifications block repeats Max Lift Height 15', Payload Capacity 4,000 lbs, Maximum Automatic Speed 5 mph, Forks 'ITA Rated; 42\" Standard, 36\"-72\" Optional'. Corroborated by /forkables/ page and by MODEX 2024 launch coverage (Modern Materials Handling, DC Velocity).
CONVERSIONS: 4000 lb = 1814.37 -> 1814 kg. 15 ft = 4572 mm exactly. 5 mph = 2.2352 -> 2.24 m/s.
PLAUSIBILITY: 4572 mm / 1814 kg is within the normal counterbalanced-class envelope; Seegrid markets it as 'industry-leading combination of height and capacity' for autonomous lift trucks, and FAQ notes 'a mast that supports future capabilities for higher heights' - i.e. 15 ft is the current certified maximum, not a mast limit.
navigation_type + infrastructure_free: page section 'Infrastructure-Free - Seegrid AMRs utilize infrastructure-free LiDAR SLAM and Grid Engine localization' plus '3D Computer Vision' section. Most explicit nav statement of the four models. HIGH.
autonomous_charging: page section 'Synchronized Self-Charging ... Auto-Charge automates fleet scheduling, dispatch, and charging'. HIGH.
manual_usage: FAQ 'Can the CR1 be manually operated? Yes, all of our AMRs are hybrid ... allow for manual or autonomous operations.' Also 'ride-on flexibility' (RS1 FAQ). HIGH.
safety_coverage: MEDIUM-HIGH. Not phrased as '360 degrees' on the CR1 page, but the FAQ states CR1 uses 'the same core LiDAR/SLAM and 3D computer vision sensor suites' as the RS1, and the CR1 safety block lists the identical '(5) 2D and 3D LiDAR sensors'. /safety/ page describes the ENTIRE fleet as maintaining 'continuous, real-time, three-dimensional awareness ... around the robot and its payload'.
station_applications: 'Standard rack' IS set for the CR1 (unlike EL1/RS1) because the page explicitly names 'vertical placement', 'vertical storage operations' and 'vertical putaway' at 15 ft - that is racking, not bulk floor storage. MEDIUM-HIGH.
autonomous_obstacle_bypass: deliberately NOT set. The CR1's 'Dynamic Path Planning' section describes 'real-time alignment adjustments to better handle poorly placed payloads' - that is payload alignment, not obstacle bypass. No 'adjusts its route around obstacles' claim exists on the CR1 page.
OTHER PUBLISHED FACTS not mappable to AP0: 5 safety-rated 2D/3D LiDAR sensors, 3 emergency stops, LED lightbar, acoustic warning system, 'Sliding Scale Autonomy' (Seegrid's AMR/AGV hybrid behaviour model), Modern Materials Handling Product of the Year.

TWO SOURCES, DIFFERENT RELIABILITY - read carefully.

(A) HIGH CONFIDENCE - current product page https://seegrid.com/autonomous-mobile-robots/tow-tractor-s7-amr/ (retrieved 2026-08-01):
Hero "10,000 LB LOAD CAPACITY | 4.0 MPH"; Technical Details 'Maximum Capacity: 10,000 lbs', 'Maximum Automatic Speed: 4 mph'; Safety 'ANSI/ITSDF B56.5-2019 / ANSI B11.0', 'UL 583 certified'. FAQ 'Tow Tractor can operate on inclines up to 2.5%'. FAQ on trailers: 'The S7 is limited by weight, not cart train length ... it can tow any number of carts ... provided the total load capacity does not exceed 10,000 lbs.' Page: 'the Tow Tractor S7 can be equipped with Auto-Charge and Auto-Hitch'. Navigation: 'proprietary 3D computer vision navigation system' + 'Infrastructure-Free - Seegrid AMRs navigate with computer-vision technology'.
CONVERSIONS: 10000 lb x 0.45359237 = 4535.92 -> 4536 kg. 4 mph x 0.44704 = 1.78816 -> 1.79 m/s.
towing_capacity used (not max_payload): the FAQ is explicit that the S7 'does not lift pallets ... it is an automated tugger designed to hitch to and tow wheeled cart trains'. A deck payload rating is not published, so max_payload left NULL.
max_trailers left NULL deliberately: Seegrid states there is NO cart-count limit, only the 10,000 lb weight limit. Any integer here would be wrong.
navigation_type = ['Vision'] only. SLAM is NOT claimed on the S7 page (unlike EL1/CR1) - the 2D/3D LiDAR is described under Safety, not navigation. Not carried over from the Lift models.
safety_standard: 'UL 583' was NOT mapped to AP0's 'UL 3100'. UL 583 is the electrical safety standard for electric industrial trucks; UL 3100 is the AGV/AMR standard. Mapping them would be a fabrication.
route_programming 'Teach-in': archived brochure 'Route transfer between robots: train one and transfer route knowledge to all' - Seegrid's trained-route model. MEDIUM-HIGH.
route_type deliberately left NULL: Seegrid describes 'Sliding Scale Autonomy ... blends the agility of AMRs and the predictability of AGVs' and 'route changes can be made while production is running'. That sits between AP0's 'Fixed Route' and 'Flexible Route' - no defensible single choice.
coupling_type ['Automatic'] / auto_hitch true: from 'Auto-Hitch for payload engagement' (brochure) and 'can be equipped with ... Auto-Hitch' (current page). NOTE: Auto-Hitch is described as an OPTION, not standard - auto_hitch is a Cond. K.O. field, so confirm optionality is acceptable for the tender before relying on it.

(B) LOW CONFIDENCE - ARCHIVED brochure, possible generation drift. Source: Wayback Machine copy of https://hub.seegrid.com/hubfs/Palion%20Tow%20Tractor%20Brochure.pdf (the live URL is dead; this is the PALION-branded predecessor of the S7). Its 'PRODUCT SPECIFICATIONS' page states verbatim: Maximum Capacity 10,000 lbs; Maximum Automatic Speed up to 4.0 mph, Reverse -0.7 mph; Width 36\"; Height 76\"; Length 60\"; Turning Radius automatic outside min 96\", manual outside min 46\"; Weight 1,860 lbs; Wheels Rubber; Battery 24V, max capacity 840 Amp-hr, compartment 31\"x13\"x32\", connector Red SB-175, weight 854-1,500 lbs, 'Change roll deck: Standard'; Environment 'Only indoor operation', Temperature 32 degF min / 104 degF max, Humidity 20-95% RH non-condensing; Safety ANSI/ITSDF B56.5-2019, ANSI B11.0, ISO 13849 category 3 emergency stops; Auto-Charge works with EnerSys NexSys Thin Plate Pure Lead (TPPL) batteries.
WHY IT IS PROBABLY STILL THE SAME VEHICLE: capacity (10,000 lbs) and max automatic speed (4.0 mph) match the CURRENT S7 page EXACTLY, and the safety standard list matches exactly. WHY IT IS STILL FLAGGED LOW: the brochure predates the S7 naming, and Seegrid has since shipped a 'Series 8' tow tractor generation advertised with 'a shorter clearance height' and 'extended field of view' - so height, sensors and possibly length may have changed.
CONVERSIONS from (B): 36 in = 914.4 -> 914 mm; 60 in = 1524 mm; 96 in = 2438.4 -> 2438 mm (automatic-mode outside turning radius - the manual 46\" figure is NOT applicable to autonomous operation); 32 degF = 0 degC; 104 degF = 40 degC; humidity max 95 %.
battery_type ['Lead-Acid']: EnerSys NexSys TPPL = Thin Plate Pure Lead, which IS a lead-acid chemistry (not Li-Ion). Named explicitly in the brochure. Confidence MED for chemistry, LOW for currency.
battery_swap_capable true: LOW-MED inference from 'Change roll deck: Standard' plus a defined battery compartment (31x13x32 in), an SB-175 connector and a min/max battery weight range - that is a classic roll-out battery-change deck. Flagged as an inference, not a quoted spec.
outdoor_capable false: brochure 'Environment: Only indoor operation' - explicit, but from source (B).
autonomous_obstacle_bypass deliberately left NULL: brochure Standard Safety Behaviors say 'Stops if it detects an object in the primary personnel or secondary object detection systems and resumes travel once object is removed' -> that is stop-and-wait, i.e. FALSE for the Palion generation. But the current S7 page makes no such statement and the newer Lift models do claim route adjustment. Setting false risks a wrong disqualification on a stale fact; NULL is safer.
intersection_management deliberately left NULL: brochure lists 'Timed pauses at intersections where other traffic has right of way' under TRAINED behaviours - a taught pause, not managed traffic control.
floor_flatness_req left NULL: brochure only gives qualitative guidance ('floors should not be uneven/cracked', 'free from oils, moisture, debris') - no FM/F-number class.
NOT FOUND (left NULL): tugger_min_aisle_width, load_transfer, trailer_compatibility, trailer_steering_technology, auto_hitch_position_tolerance, battery_runtime, charge_time (brochure says only 'fast charge in just over an hour' for TPPL - too vague), max_fleet_size, vda5050_compatible, stop_accuracy, ingress_protection_rating.
